items.followUp: What type of intermolecular forces act between water molecules?

rubric.why: Shows that HCl molecules have permanent dipoles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that HCl is polar.

rubric.why: Names the attractive force between polar HCl molecules.
rubric.description: Names the intermolecular force as dipole–dipole attraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying dipole–dipole forces.

modelAnswer: Therefore, dipole–dipole forces exist between HCl molecules.

items.followUp: Define isotopes and give one example.

rubric.why: States the defining feature of allotropy.
rubric.description: Defines allotropy as an element existing in different forms in the same physical state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including different forms and the same physical state in the definition.

rubric.why: Gives a valid example of allotropy.
rubric.description: Names a valid example, such as diamond and graphite as forms of carbon.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a correct example of allotropes.

modelAnswer: Allotropy is the property of an element to exist in two or more different forms in the same physical state.
For example, carbon exists as diamond and graphite.
